digest.component_or_area: Process-local caches and shared temp artifact isolation
propositions: Six cache/temp write sites in src/rebar derive non-unique names from content hashes, pids, or fixed literals, causing concurrent writers to share temp pathnames and collide on replace or observe torn reads.

The completion_verdict_cache exemplar in commit 89981d8e and the existing fsutil.atomic_write helper (118 LOC, ~50 call sites) implement the correct pattern but five other sites remain unconverted, each vulnerable to FileNotFoundError or partial file observability.

Sites review_bot/reconcile.py:177, _config_writer.py:279, _cli/__init__.py:253, and _opcert_signing.py:77 use process-derived or fixed-literal temp suffixes and shared os.replace without atomic write; _snapshot/janitor.py:300 and completion_banking.py:507 write directly without temp intermediary, allowing torn reads.
All module-level caches and lru_cache instances in src/rebar are already keyed by absolute path, repo root, or stat token; no root-unkeyed caches exist to fix.
Conversion to fsutil.atomic_write across all six sites closes both the collision window and the torn-read window without adding new modules or helpers.
